findings.title: Four configured transitions, but only one state-machine insertion point and one status pair
findings.description:
- The `[workflow.review_gates]` table (lines 81–86) defines `pre-tasks`, `pre-implementation` and `pre-advance` as v1 slice-level gates.
- Everything else only describes the `pre-advance` case:
  - `pending-review` is defined as "tasks complete … no review artifact present" (line 106).
  - The only insertion point is "between current Priority 5 (`in-implementation`) and Priority 6 (`complete → advance`)" (line 115).
  - The sample rationale hard-codes `type: code` (line 118).
  - Anticipated Slice 2 (line 159) adds one priority branch.
- Nothing says how `pre-tasks` works. That would mean blocking the Priority 4 `needs-tasks` recommendation (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:224`) until a `slice` review clears.
- Nothing says how `pre-implementation` works:
  - Is it in force while `in-implementation` has 0 tasks checked?
  - Does checking the first box bypass it?
  - What status does the slice show? `pending-review` is defined as "tasks complete", so it can't be reused here.
- Line 141 says "V1 implements only the **four** slice-level transitions", but only three slice-level transitions are listed. The fourth (`pre-slice-plan`) is explicitly deferred.

As written, an implementer can only build `pre-advance`. The other two gates would be accepted in config but do nothing. Either define where each gate sits in the cascade and what status it produces, or cut v1 to `pre-advance` only.

findings.title: The shared navigator can't read config, so "inherited by both surfaces without per-surface work" is false
findings.description:
- Line 34 says the gate lives in `WorkflowNavigator`/`ConsistencyChecker` and both surfaces inherit it with no per-surface work.
- In the actual code, none of the three components can see config:
  - `WorkflowNavigator` is stateless. `getNext(project: ProjectData)` and `deriveSliceStatus(project, projectPath)` take no config.
  - `ConsistencyChecker`'s constructor takes only an `IArtifactIntrospector` (`ConsistencyChecker.ts:37`).
  - `detectDocuments(projectPath, sliceIndex)` takes no `reviewType`, but line 131 needs it to match "for the … configured reviewType".
- The only existing workflow key, `workflow.auto_fix`, is read separately by each surface: `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:141` and `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/workflowTools.ts:263`. That is the opposite of what the document claims.

The design needs an explicit decision, for example:
- Inject a resolved `ReviewGateConfig` into the `getNext`/`getStatus`/`check` signatures, which means every caller changes; or
- Have the core build a `ConfigManager(project.projectPath)` itself. This puts a config→introspection dependency into a component that is currently pure.

`getStatus()` also calls `deriveSliceStatus`, so `workflow_status` and `cf status` are affected too. The document never mentions them.

findings.title: With gating enabled and no `review_gates` table, it's unclear which transitions are gated
findings.description:
- Line 30 promises "sensible defaults". Line 88 says `review_threshold` applies "when no per-transition override exists". Line 111 says nothing is set when "no gate is configured for the current transition".
- So suppose someone sets only `workflow.review_enabled = true`. Is `pre-advance` gated, with a default `reviewType = "code"`? Are all four gated? Is nothing gated?
- This is load-bearing: it decides whether turning on the global switch does anything at all.
- Also undefined: what happens if a table entry omits `reviewType`, or names an unknown transition key? Line 48 claims fail-fast but gives no schema.

findings.title: The threshold and `review_unknown_as` values are never listed and are used inconsistently
findings.description:
- The allowed values of `review_threshold` are never listed. Line 95 says CONCERNS clears if the threshold is "`concerns` or lower", but no value lower than `concerns` exists (`fail`? `none`?).
- `review_unknown_as` values are inconsistent across the document:
  - Line 75 gives `"fail"`.
  - Line 147 uses `"concern"` (singular), while the threshold vocabulary uses `"concerns"`.
  - Line 106 implies a third value that maps UNKNOWN to `pending-review` ("`review_unknown_as` treats it as pending").
- The `enum` arrays in `ConfigKeyDefinition` can't be written until these are fixed.
- The `pending-review` rationale (line 118) says "no review artifact found". That is wrong whenever the artifact exists but its verdict is UNKNOWN.

findings.title: The "fail-fast" config validation claim doesn't match how `ConfigManager` works
findings.description:
- Line 48 names `ConfigKeyDefinition.validate` as the place invalid values get caught.
- But `validateValue` only runs inside `ConfigManager.set()` (`ConfigManager.ts:145`). `get()` returns whatever `resolveKey` finds, with no type, enum or validator check.
- So a hand-edited `.context-forge.toml` containing `review_threshold = "strict"` reaches the gate unvalidated. That is exactly the silent pass/block that line 48 forbids.
- `get()` also throws `Unknown config key` for anything not registered in `CONFIG_KEYS`, and `type` only allows `'string' | 'boolean' | 'number'`.
- Line 145 leaves the nested-vs-flat decision for `review_gates` open. The read-path validation gap exists under either choice.
- Recommendation: validate when config is read in the gate, using a dedicated `ReviewGateConfig` loader that parses the whole `workflow.review_*` subtree once. Don't try to force inline tables into `ConfigKeyDefinition`.

findings.title: The existing frontmatter parser can't support the planned failure handling or field carriage
findings.description:
- Line 149 requires the rationale to "name the parse failure explicitly" (malformed YAML, encoding, permission error).
- But `parseFrontmatter` (`frontmatterParser.ts:9-49`) never throws. Every failure collapses to `{ found: false, data: {} }`, so a permission error, a missing closing `---` and an absent `verdict` all look the same.
- It's also a flat line-by-line `key: value` splitter typed as `Record<string, string>`:
  - `score` arrives as a string.
  - Nested `criteria`/`provenance` (line 46: "carries … as opaque fields") get shredded into bogus top-level keys, because list items such as `- name: x` become keys.
- The document needs to say whether the gate gets a real YAML parse (a new dependency or an existing one) or a review-specific reader that reports errors.
- Related: `deriveSliceStatus` wraps everything in `catch { return base; }` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:494`). An exception while reading the review would downgrade the slice to `no-active-slice` rather than UNKNOWN. That breaks line 98's guarantee.

findings.title: One `review` detection slot, keyed by slice index, can't serve multiple review types or the arch gate
findings.description:
- Line 131 adds a single `review: string | null` slot. But one slice can need `slice`, `tasks` and `code` reviews at different stages.
- With one slot, the detector has to know which transition is current (a navigator concern leaking into the detector), or it gets called once per type.
- The slot should be a map such as `reviews: Partial<Record<ReviewType, string>>`, returned without needing config.
- `pre-slice-plan` needs `NNN-review.arch.*` keyed on the **arch** index (line 141). `detectDocuments` is keyed on the active slice index, and in that flow no slice is active: it's the Priority 2 branch.
- Line 131 says "the existing naming convention (e.g., `210-review.code…`)" and "no new convention is introduced". In this repo there is no `project-documents/user/reviews/` directory and no review artifact. The only trace is a test fixture, `181-review.slice.foo.md`, in `frontmatterSchema.test.ts:226`. The convention is assumed, not established here.

findings.title: Picking the "lexicographically last" match does not give the most recent review
findings.description:
- The naming pattern is `NNN-review.{type}.{slug}.md`, and in the cited example the slug is the slice name (`github-copilot-vs-code-ide-support`). There's no date or sequence number.
- Re-running a review either overwrites the same filename, so there's nothing to choose between, or produces a different slug whose sort order has nothing to do with time.
- Line 133 calls the result "most recent by sort order". That's deterministic, but it can pick a stale FAIL over a newer PASS. In the fail → re-review → pass loop that line 109 explicitly expects, this produces wrong routing.
- Either require a sortable suffix in the Squadron contract, or define the rule as "a single artifact per (index, type); duplicates produce a consistency error".

findings.title: The new rule conflicts with existing auto-fixable consistency rules and floods historical slices
findings.description:
- Existing rule `task-vs-plan` (`ConsistencyChecker.ts:269-282`) auto-fixes by **checking** the slice-plan entry as soon as tasks are complete.
- Existing rule `frontmatter-vs-computed` (`:338+`) sets frontmatter `status: complete` under the same condition.
- Neither rule knows about reviews. With `auto_fix`, `cf check` would mark a gated slice complete in the plan and then, in the same run, report the new "marked complete … but review absent" warning (line 137).
- The plan checkbox then makes Priority 6's `find((e) => !e.isChecked)` skip past it.
- The document has to decide whether `pending-review`/`review-failed` slices should be left unchecked and non-complete in plan and frontmatter. That means changing two existing rules, which contradicts "purely additive" (line 167).
- `checkAll` covers every slice in every plan. Turning gating on in an established project would flag every historical slice that lacks a review. The rule needs a scope, such as active slice only or slices completed after enablement.

findings.title: Recommendation vocabulary and payload don't match the existing `NextAction` contract
findings.description:
- Every existing `recommendation` is human-readable prose: "Advance to slice …", "Continue implementation — N tasks remaining" (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:240,253`).
- Lines 118/124 introduce bare tokens `"review"`/`"blocked"`. Line 173 then claims Amoeba depends on "a stable vocabulary" of `recommendation` values. No such vocabulary exists, and mixing tokens with prose makes the field harder to parse, not easier.
- A runner routing to a review agent needs the `reviewType`, the gate, the verdict and the artifact path. With no new fields on `NextAction` (line 173 forbids changing it), all of that is only in the rationale prose. That defeats the line 32 goal of acting "without parsing recommendation strings".
- Adding optional fields (for example `gate?: { transition, reviewType, verdict, artifactPath }`) is backward-compatible and should be allowed.
- Line 167 says "no 160 interfaces change", but `SliceStatus['status']` and `DocumentDetectionResult` are 160 interfaces, and both change.

findings.title: The worktree-scoped config resolution it relies on doesn't exist
findings.description:
- Line 171 says initiative 180 "established worktree-scoped config resolution" and that review keys should use "the resolution chain 180 introduced".
- 180's resolution chain is CWD → project/context *identity* resolution (`180-arch…md:116-124`), not config.
- `ConfigManager` resolves only project → user → default. It reads `{projectPath}/.context-forge.toml` (`configPaths.ts:10`), where `projectPath` is the registered main path, so a worktree-local TOML is never read.
- Per-initiative review policy is new work and needs to be scoped or deferred explicitly. As written, it's an assumed capability.

findings.title: Over-built for v1: cut the score path, field carriage, per-gate table, and unimplemented gate keys
findings.description:
The requirement is "don't recommend advance when the review is missing or failing". Several mechanisms go beyond that with no v1 consumer:
- **Cut:** reading and "storing" `score` (line 100), plus a "documented code path" for enforcement. There's no field to store it in, and that branch would never run until Squadron 301 exists.
- **Cut:** carrying `criteria`/`provenance` as opaque fields (line 46). Nothing in CF consumes them, and the flat parser would mangle them anyway.
- **Defer:** `review_unknown_as` (line 75). Hard-coding UNKNOWN → fail matches the stated "conservative" principle, and the knob creates the support confusion line 147 already admits to.
- **Defer:** the four-entry `[workflow.review_gates]` table (lines 81–86). Ship `pre-advance` with `review_threshold` plus a single `review_type` key. The table is what forces the unresolved nested-config question in line 145.
- Defining `pre-slice-plan` in the config schema while its logic is deferred (line 141) means projects can configure a gate that silently does nothing. That's the silent pass line 48 forbids. Reject the key until it's implemented.

findings.title: Which slice does the priority renumbering is stated two different ways
findings.description: Line 151 says "the slice implementing the gate logic should renumber the full cascade". Line 157 puts renumbering in the first slice (discovery/config), which "has no gate logic yet". Pick one. Renumbering without the new branch is churn with no purpose.

findings.title: `auto_advance` has no consumer in the code
findings.description: The reasoning in line 153 holds. But `workflow.auto_advance` is only defined (`ConfigKeys.ts:26`) and never read anywhere in `packages/`, so "the gate naturally takes precedence" is true trivially. No action needed. Just don't use it as evidence that the gate composes with existing runner behaviour.
